quadriceps femoris muscle: Powerful knee extensor made up of rectus femoris and the three vasti; inserts into the patella and, through the patellar ligament, into the tibia. Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
radial collateral ligament: Fan-shaped ligament from the lateral epicondyle to the annular ligament; resists varus stress.
radial collateral ligament of wrist join: Ligament from the radial styloid process to the scaphoid.
radial fossa: Small anterior fossa above the capitulum; the radial head enters it when the elbow is flexed.
radial groove: Spiral groove on the back of the humeral shaft; the radial nerve and profunda brachii artery run in it.
radial head of flexor digitorum superfic: Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis
Arises from the front of the radius; the muscle's tendons insert into the middle phalanges and flex the PIP joints. Median nerve.
radial notch: Notch on the lateral side of the coronoid process; forms the proximal radio-ulnar joint with the radial head.
radial styloid process: Process at the lower lateral end of the radius; brachioradialis inserts into it, and it lies lower than the ulnar styloid.
radial tuberosity: Prominence below the neck; the biceps brachii tendon inserts here.
radiate carpal ligament: Palmar ligament radiating like a star from the head of the capitate to the surrounding carpal bones.
radiate ligament of head of rib: Radiate ligament of head of rib
Ligament fanning out from the rib head to two vertebral bodies and the disc.
radiocapitate ligament: Part of the palmar radiocarpal ligaments running from the radius to the capitate.
radioscaphocapitate ligament: Ligament passing across the waist of the scaphoid to the capitate; it provides the axis of rotation of the scaphoid.
radius: Forearm bone on the thumb (lateral) side; by rotating around the ulna it produces pronation and supination. A fracture of its distal end (Colles') is the commonest wrist fracture.
rectus abdominis muscle: Muscle running from the pubis to the 5th–7th costal cartilages and the xiphoid, divided by 3–4 tendinous intersections (the 'six-pack'). It lies within the rectus sheath. Nerves: T7–T12. It flexes the trunk.
rectus anterior capitis muscle: Short prevertebral muscle from the atlas to the occipital bone; flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.
rectus femoris muscle: The only head of quadriceps that also crosses the hip; arises from the AIIS, flexes the hip and extends the knee. Femoral nerve.
rectus lateralis capitis muscle: Runs from the transverse process of the atlas to the jugular process of the occipital bone; tilts the head sideways.
rectus posterior major capitis muscle: Suboccipital muscle from the spine of the axis to the occipital bone; extends and rotates the head. Suboccipital nerve (C1).
rectus posterior minor capitis muscle: Runs from the posterior tubercle of the atlas to the occiput; its connection to the dura has been linked to tension-type headache.
rhomboid major muscle: Runs from the T2–T5 spines to the medial border of the scapula; retracts the scapula. Nerve: dorsal scapular nerve.
rhomboid minor muscle: Small muscle from the C7–T1 spines to the level of the root of the spine of the scapula.
rib: Curved bone of the thoracic cage; it continues in front as the costal cartilage.
risorius muscle: Pulls the corner of the mouth sideways; contributes to dimples.
root apex: Tip of the root; nerves and vessels enter the tooth through the apical foramen.
root of tooth: Part of the tooth embedded in the alveolus; covered with cementum.
rotatores: The deepest small muscles, running from a transverse process to the base of the lamina one or two levels above; they contribute to proprioception during spinal movement.
sacral canal: Continuation of the vertebral canal in the sacrum; it contains the lower roots of the cauda equina and the filum terminale.
sacral hiatus: Opening at the lower posterior end of the sacrum; caudal epidural anaesthesia is given here.
sacral horn: Horns on each side of the hiatus; they guide caudal block.
sacral tuberosity: Rough area behind the auricular surface; the interosseous sacroiliac ligaments attach to it.
sacrococcygeal symphysis: Fibrocartilaginous joint between the tip of the sacrum and the coccyx; it lets the coccyx bend backwards during childbirth.
sacropelvic surface of ilium: Inner posterior surface of the ilium facing the sacrum and pelvis.
sacrospinous ligament: Triangular ligament from the edge of the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine; it separates the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.
sacrotuberous ligament: Strong ligament from the sacrum to the ischial tuberosity; prevents the sacrum tipping forwards and bounds the lesser sciatic foramen.
sacrum: Triangular bone formed by the fusion of five sacral vertebrae; it forms the back wall of the pelvis between the two hip bones. Branches of the sacral nerves emerge through the anterior and posterior sacral foramina.
sagittal border of parietal bone: Border forming the sagittal suture with the opposite parietal.
sartorius muscle: The longest muscle in the body; runs from the ASIS to the medial surface of the tibia (pes anserinus). It flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip and flexes the knee. Femoral nerve.
scalenus anterior muscle: Runs from the C3–C6 transverse processes to the 1st rib; the phrenic nerve and subclavian vein pass in front of it, the subclavian artery and brachial plexus behind (scalene gap). It raises the 1st rib.
scalenus medius muscle: The largest scalene; runs from the cervical vertebrae to the 1st rib, and the roots of the long thoracic nerve pass through it.
scalenus posterior muscle: The smallest scalene, from the lower cervical vertebrae to the 2nd rib; raises the rib in deep inspiration.
scaphoid bone: The most lateral and largest bone of the proximal carpal row; it is felt in the anatomical snuffbox. Because its blood supply comes from distally, avascular necrosis of the proximal fragment can follow waist fractures.
scaphoid fossa: Fossa above the medial plate; tensor veli palatini arises here.
scapholunate interosseous ligament: The most important carpal ligament, joining the scaphoid and lunate; when it tears a gap opens (Terry-Thomas sign) and a DISI deformity develops.
scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal ligament: Binds the distal end of the scaphoid to the trapezium and trapezoid.
scapula: Triangular flat bone on the upper back of the thoracic cage; it carries the spine, acromion, coracoid process and glenoid cavity, and gives attachment to 17 muscles.
scapular notch: Notch on the upper border; the suprascapular nerve passes beneath it and the suprascapular artery above.
scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle: Posterior fibres; move the arm backwards and rotate it laterally.
sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus muscle: Over the ischial tuberosity; it becomes inflamed in people who sit for long periods.
sciatic bursa of obturator internus: Bursa beneath the tendon as it turns over the lesser sciatic notch.
second metacarpal bone: The 2nd of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.
second metatarsal bone: The 2nd of the five long bones of the metatarsus; its base articulates with the tarsal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.
